title: Delta ledger backfill and fuzzy-match audit for partial streaming claims
creator: Maya Patel
description: Investigate and implement a robust backfill + audit process for streaming sessions where final token counts are missing or inconsistent due to partial disconnects, client retries, or gateway upgrades. The goal is to produce a delta-ledger approach that can (a) compute a minimal set of adjustments to user ledgers without double-charging, (b) produce a verifiable fuzzy-match audit report for ops and finance, and (c) expose safe runbooks for automated corrections when confidence is high.
motivation: We continue to see infrequent but high-impact discrepancies between session micrologs and billing ledgers after mid-stream model handoffs, intermittent gateway timeouts, and client-side chunk reordering. Manual investigations are expensive and leave customers with confusing invoices. A deterministic backfill that tolerates slight variations in tokenization counts and partial payload echoes will reduce false positives and write-offs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A backfill job can consume archived stream micrologs and produce an adjustment delta set for any given customer session id with confidence score metadata.
2) Adjustments are idempotent: applying the same delta twice does not change ledger totals after first application.
3) Fuzzy-match auditing report enumerates candidate reasons (replay, duplicate frame, tokenization drift, model-switch) with sample evidence and a computed confidence percentage.

4) End-to-end test harness demonstrates correction on three synthetic failure modes: (A) mid-stream model failover, (B) out-of-order fragments from a mobile client, (C) reconnect that replayed last N frames.
5) Backfill is rate-limited and runs with a circuit-breaker; when adjustment confidence < 60% require manual review and create incident ticket.
6) Documentation and ops runbook published in Confluence with CLI for review/rollback.
7) No customer-facing invoices altered without audit trail and PM approval for high-impact (> $500) adjustments.
8) Performance: backfill job completes for a 7-day bucket containing 100k sessions within 90 minutes on staging sized workers.
design_notes: We will adopt a delta-ledger event model: compute per-session candidate deltas (positive or negative token counts) rather than rewriting original ledgers.

Fuzzy matching will use three signals: (1) chronological microlog overlap, (2) prompt+response approximate token fingerprint (normalized whitespace + hash of first/last 64 bytes after tokenizer normalization), (3) session pedigree metadata like client-id, SDK version, and routing node.
Confidence scoring heuristic: weighted aggregation of signals with adjustable weights stored in config; initial weights: time_overlap=0.45, fingerprint=0.35, pedigree=0.2.
Idempotency: tag generated deltas with deterministic UUID derived from session id + window start + canonicalized microlog hash so re-run deduplicates.
Safety: deltas with confidence >= 90% auto-apply; 60-89% create review queue; <60% are flagged for manual analysis only.
Storage: use archived micrologs stored in S3 bucket s3://redwood-micrologs/streams/YYYY-MM for input; deltas are written to billing-adjustments table with audit columns.
Backfill orchestration: airflow DAG prototype, but implement a bulletproof single-run job first (k8s job) for rapid testing.
Testing: synthetic harness will produce golden logs representing each failure mode and expected delta outputs. We'll include negative tests for duplicate application and clock skew.
Metrics: create grafana dashboard for backfill throughput, avg confidence, auto-apply rate, manual-review queue length, and total outstanding delta amount.
Rollout: staged behind feature flag. Start with internal accounts, then small customer cohort, then org-wide.
Fallback: if ledger divergence > 5% of expected monthly spend for a single org, pause auto-apply and escalate to Billing SME.
Compliance: ensure audit trail includes user-visible explanation and original microlog excerpt when any adjustment is applied.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Build microlog ingestion job and canonical microlog normalizer (Maya, Jun).
Week 2: Implement fuzzy fingerprinting library and confidence scorer (Liam).
Week 3: Delta generation pipeline, deterministic id generation, and write-to-adjustments table (Liam, Sana).
Week 4: Auto-apply logic with safety checks, idempotency tests, and basic CLI to inspect deltas (Sana).
Week 5: Integrate audit report generation and Confluence ops runbook; create Grafana dashboards and schedule manual review queue (Maya, Ops).
Week 6: Run internal backfill on 7-day staging bucket; collect metrics and iterate, then enable feature flag for small external cohort.
Contingency: if idempotency failures observed, immediate rollback of auto-apply and migration to manual review only while root cause is fixed.
open_questions: Should the confidence scorer incorporate tokenizer model-specific differences (e.g., gpt2 vs. new open tokenizer) or normalize by converting to a canonical tokenizer first?
Do we allow negative adjustments beyond invoice period boundaries (e.g., retroactive credits crossing billing cycle)? Finance requested soft-limits.
Is it acceptable to store first/last 64 bytes of normalized text in adjustments table for audit, or do we need encryption/PII review?
What's the SLA for manual review turnaround? Finance suggests 3 business days for any adjustment > $100.
Where to run the heavy microlog diffs: k8s job in runtime cluster vs batch workers in separate billing cluster?
tests: Synthetic failure generator for three modes: model-switch, out-of-order fragments, replayed reconnect. Produces input micrologs + expected delta set.
Property-based tests asserting idempotency of delta application and non-negativity of customer token balance unless explicit crediting rule applies.
E2E staging run with 7-day bucket (100k sessions) validating performance SLA and audit report integrity.
Chaos test: inject clock skew up to +/- 120s and validate fuzzy-match resilience and no double charges.
Security test: verify microlog excerpts stored in adjustment audit are redacted for PII; run manual review of excerpts.
